summary: Best state b7877ce408033954: a source rewrite to loop-free threads (one element per thread, grid cdiv(N,256) x block 256, the strided per-thread loop removed, the double libm pow replaced by a hoisted integer power by squaring in double, bias corrections/step size/sqrt(bc2) computed once) followed by coarsen factor 2. Measured 1.090x over amdclang (95% CI 1.088-1.092, 240 pairs; 0.334 ms vs 0.365 ms), full battery 49/49. 1.5x is out of reach: the kernel is memory-bound. With amsgrad=0 it really touches 4 input and 3 output tensors (1.07 GB read, 0.81 GB written), whose floor by the notes' model is 20 us + 238 us + 75 us = about 333 us; the baseline is at 349-376 us (true headroom about 1.05-1.1) and the best state sits at 330-335 us, i.e. on the floor. Every element is touched exactly once, so there are no fewer bytes to move. Results meet the manifest tolerance, not bit-identity (integer pow instead of libm pow).

friction: bench's traffic model counts every manifest tensor (9 tensors: 1610 MB read, 1074 MB written) although with amsgrad=0 the two max_exp_avg_sq tensors are never touched; the reported memory_floor (0.478 ms) is above the measured time and headroom comes out as 0.7-0.78, which is meaningless. I had to recompute the floor by hand (333 us). A way to declare tensors as untouched for the benched scalar values, or a traffic count derived from the executed loads/stores, would fix it.

The reference time moved between 0.346 and 0.376 ms across consecutive bench calls (clock level 471-1139 MHz), so speedups against ref from separate 60-pair runs were not comparable (the same state measured 1.045x and 1.090x); only compare(a, b, pairs=240) ranked candidates reliably. A bench that times several candidates in one interleaved process would save many launches.

source(like=...) required a dummy define (BLK) to make a block-size variant distinct, since only the launch changed; relaunch would have been the right tool but I only noticed afterwards - a hint in the source() error/description would help.

pow(float, uint32) in the baseline compiles to about 450 double-precision instructions per thread; a loop-free restructuring is impossible without replacing it. There is no way to pass a host-computed scalar derived from the manifest's scalar parameters (launch args are expressions over shape symbols only), so it had to be recomputed per thread by squaring.
lessons: mo_adam (4 streams read, 3 written, 4 bytes per lane, N = 2^26): amdclang's build of the library's strided per-thread loop (1024 workgroups x 256 iterations, stride 1 MB, one load group per wait) already runs within 5-10% of the memory floor (349-376 us against 20 us + read/4.5 + written/10.7 = 333 us). Loop-free threads gave 1.065x, plus coarsen 2 gave 1.09x in total (330-335 us = the floor). Nothing more is available without touching fewer bytes.

Elements per thread on a 7-stream elementwise kernel, block 256: 1 element 1.065x, 2 elements 1.017x better than 1 (240-pair compare), 4 elements 1.04x vs ref (worse than 1 or 2). Coarsen 2 on the 1-element state: +2.9%; coarsen 4: 3.6% worse than coarsen 2; coarsen 2 on the 2-element state: 3.5% worse than coarsen 2 on the 1-element state. So about 2 KB of each stream per workgroup (512 elements) is the optimum, reached either way, and 4 KB is past it.
Block size for the loop-free 1-element kernel: 256 best (1.065x), 64 1.026x, 1024 a loss (0.975x).

A libm pow(float, uint) in a library kernel costs about 450 f64 instructions per thread; replacing it by a square-and-multiply loop in double (wave-uniform exponent, 4 iterations for step = 10) passes a 1e-4 tolerance on all 49 battery cases and makes one-element-per-thread structures affordable.
The reference time floats by up to 8% between bench calls (clock level changes): rank candidates with compare(a, b, pairs=240), not through separate speedups against ref.
bench's headroom is wrong when a flag-guarded tensor is never touched (here it reported 0.7): recompute the floor from the tensors the benched configuration really reads and writes.

session.final:
The best verified state is `b7877ce408033954`, at **1.090x** over amdclang (95% CI 1.088–1.092, 240 pairs; 0.334 ms against 0.365 ms), battery 49/49. The 1.5x target is out of reach for this kernel, and the report is filed.

- **What it does:** a source rewrite to loop-free threads — one element per thread, grid `cdiv(N, 256)` × block 256 — with the bias corrections, step size and `sqrt(bc2)` computed once per thread, then `coarsen` factor 2. The library's double-precision `pow` is replaced by an integer power by squaring, so results meet the manifest tolerance but are not bit-identical to the baseline.
- **Why not 1.5x:** the kernel is memory-bound and touches every element exactly once. With `amsgrad=0` it reads 4 tensors and writes 3, which gives a floor of about 333 µs by the notes' model; the baseline runs at 349–376 µs and the best state at 330–335 µs, on the floor.
- **Headroom figure is wrong here:** `bench` reported headroom 0.7–0.78 because it counts the two `max_exp_avg_sq` tensors, which this configuration never touches. I recomputed the floor by hand and listed this as friction.
